packs.name: Superpowers
packs.description: A structured development workflow: brainstorm the problem first, write a plan, then execute it step by step with test-driven development, systematic debugging and verification before anything is called done. Skills trigger when relevant, so you rarely call them by name.
packs.author: Jesse Vincent (obra)

packs.name: Skills for Real Engineers
packs.description: Matt Pocock's small, focused skills for disciplined engineering with AI: grill-me interviews you one question at a time until an idea is fully thought through, to-spec, to-tickets and implement turn it into work, plus code review, TDD, diagnosing bugs, PRs and more.
packs.author: Matt Pocock

packs.name: Agent Skills
packs.description: Addy Osmani's full software lifecycle in skill form: spec, plan, build incrementally, test, review on five axes, simplify, and ship, with context engineering, security hardening, debugging and documentation along the way.
packs.author: Addy Osmani

packs.name: Karpathy Guidelines
packs.description: A short set of coding guidelines from Andrej Karpathy's observations about common LLM coding mistakes, applied quietly: surface assumptions instead of guessing, the minimum code that solves the problem, surgical changes that leave adjacent code alone, and a definition of done to verify against.
packs.author: forrestchang

packs.name: SQL Server Query Plans
packs.description: Reads SQL Server execution plans the way an experienced tuner would, from Erik Darling's own query tuning knowledge: what is actually slow and why, not which operators look expensive. Point the agent at a .sqlplan or .xml file and ask what is wrong.
packs.author: Erik Darling
